name: Kohlrabi
grown_as: Kohlrabi, a biennial grown as an annual for its swollen stem, cut when the size of a tennis ball. William grows 'Purple Vienna' (AG 72), drawn here: a purple ball and purple-stalked leaves. Green varieties such as 'Superschmelz' have a pale green ball.
habit: A short stem swollen into a ball 5 to 10 cm across just above the soil, with long-stalked leaves rising from all over its surface, the plant 30 to 45 cm high. Year 2: a branched flowering stem up to 1 m from the top of the ball.

leaf.arrangement: Alternate and spirally set around the ball, each on a long upright stalk
leaf.type: Simple; sometimes with one or two small lobes on the stalk below the blade
leaf.outline: Oval to oblong, 10 to 20 cm long
leaf.base: Narrowing into the stalk, sometimes with small lobes or wings
leaf.veins: A pale broad midrib and netted side veins
leaf.surface: Smooth, hairless, with a waxy grey bloom like cabbage
leaf.stalk: Long (10 to 20 cm), slender, upright, rising from the side of the ball, purple and leaving a crescent-shaped scar when it falls

flower.centre: Six stamens round a green style
flower.carried: In long loose spikes at the branch tips, the buds above the open flowers
flower.season: April to June of the second year

fruit: Slender cylindrical pods 5 to 10 cm with a short beak, splitting to release small round dark brown seeds.
seedling: Two kidney-shaped seed leaves notched at the tip, grey-green; stem purple in purple varieties.
winter: Not usually overwintered; harvested from summer to autumn before frost. A plant kept to flower overwinters as a ball with a few leaves.

leaf: one simple oval leaf on a long purple stalk
bloom: four pale yellow petals in a cross
seed: a tiny round dark brown seed
seedling: two kidney-shaped seed leaves notched at the tip
young: a short purple stem starting to swell above the soil
crop: a round purple ball sitting ON the soil, not in it
long purple leaf stalks rising from all over the ball's surface
scars where lower leaves have fallen
a short stem and roots below
flower: a flowering stem from the top of the ball
pale yellow cross-shaped flowers in long spikes
seedhead: slender upright beaked pods along the stems

look_alikes: Turnip and swede swell at the root, partly underground, with leaves only from the top. Cabbage and kale have the same grey leaves but no swollen stem.
